answer: Escrowed reputation decay**: each identity carries a public score that decays unless refreshed by counterparties rating completed work; cloning starts every copy at zero, and scores cannot be merged or transferred. An attacker must run each clone long enough to accumulate independent ratings, so cost scales linearly with clone count rather than once. Operators publish a comet-shaped audit trail of score refreshes; gaps trigger a saffron flag visible to all matchmakers. Fresh clones enter a slow spiral of low-value jobs before qualifying for anything profitable.
